_contract: One entry per user-facing feature, newest first; writing it is part of shipping the feature (AGENTS.md, 'What gets posted'). The same entry is the /changelog 'New on the site' list, the What's new feed and a Bluesky post (app/whats_new.py). id: a stable slug, never reused (it is the post's subject, so changing it posts again). date: the UTC day the feature reached main (git log --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%d with TZ=UTC). title: a name, no trailing period. summary: one plain sentence that stays true: no named politicians, no pronouns, no em dashes, no emoji, no year or Congress number. url: the page's path on the site. tests/test_whats_new.py checks each entry and that the post fits.

entries.title: One search for members, bills and documents
entries.summary: Site search ranks members, bills, agencies, pages and federal documents in one list, finds a document by what it is about as well as by its title, and keeps every document filter under its Documents chip.

entries.title: A page for agency budgets
entries.summary: Every federal agency's budget for the year, largest first, now has its own page under Executive, each bar linked to the agency's page.

entries.title: Presidents' portraits
entries.summary: Every president with a public-domain portrait now shows it on the page, the president list and the share card, served from this site and credited to its author.

entries.title: A president's term, drawn
entries.summary: A president's page charts the elections won, approval month by month, jobs added since the inauguration and growth in each year, each beside the other presidencies.

entries.title: Justices beside the Court
entries.summary: Each Supreme Court justice's page draws the voting record, opinions written, years served and agreement with each colleague beside every sitting justice, and links to the president who made the appointment.

entries.title: Presidents by the record
entries.summary: A president's page now draws approval, the economy and the historians' points among every other presidency with the same figure, with no 0 to 100 score.

entries.title: Member pages show figures, not scores
entries.summary: Each member page shows the money, votes and bills behind the peer comparison as the figures themselves, with no 0 to 100 scores, and the public API marks its member score fields as deprecated.

entries.title: The presidential contest
entries.summary: In a presidential year the elections page shows each state's electoral votes from the House apportionment, the candidates registered with the FEC and the primaries ahead, and calls no race.

entries.title: How the last election was run
entries.summary: Between general elections the elections page shows turnout, voting by mail and rejected mail and provisional ballots by state, from the Election Assistance Commission's survey of every election office.

entries.title: Odd-year state elections
entries.summary: Between general elections the elections page lists the states holding regular state elections in the coming odd year, with each state's election office, and says plainly what it does not cover.

entries.title: Redistricting watch
entries.summary: The new House maps page says whether the next general's maps are settled, and how each map in force got there: an act, a vote, a commission plan or a court order, with its official source.

entries.title: The next cycle's field and filing deadlines
entries.summary: Between general elections the elections page counts who has registered with the FEC for each seat, never calling a filing a place on the ballot, and leads with each FEC reporting deadline.

entries.title: How a new Congress compares
entries.summary: Once a new Congress is seated, the elections page counts the members new to each chamber, those from the other chamber, and the median age, from each member's official record.

entries.title: The elections page through the whole cycle
entries.summary: Between general elections the elections page leads with the election just held, then special elections and the calendar, then the primaries ahead, each from the law or the FEC's calendar.

entries.title: Spreadsheets of the record, and a data license
entries.summary: The leaderboards, each member's votes and every position on a roll call download as CSV, and the site states what may be reused and on what terms.

entries.title: Comparisons you can cite
entries.summary: A side-by-side comparison names the run and scoring version behind each score, shows funding diversity apart from the score, and gives a reference to cite.

entries.title: Bill pages that get to the votes
entries.summary: A bill page lists its sections under the title and keeps a long summary to its first paragraph, with the full text a tap away.

entries.title: More of the record in the public API
entries.summary: The open API and its MCP server now give every member's position on each roll call, presidents, the Supreme Court's votes case by case, nominations, agencies and the comment periods open today.

entries.title: Election stories link the ballot
entries.summary: An Action Center issue that names a race or one of its nominees now links the race, the state's next voter deadline and its official registration lookup.

entries.title: Congress at a glance, and your members' record
entries.summary: The Congress page opens with a calendar of every day each chamber sat and how far bills got, and with a state picked, that state's members' latest votes and bills.

entries.title: Search the whole site
entries.summary: One box in the header finds members, bills, agencies, districts, races, issues, documents and pages as you type, and an exact match such as a bill number goes straight to its page.

entries.title: Related votes in Congress
entries.summary: Action Center stories now list the related roll calls in Congress, with how your members voted and a call script that cites the vote, and each ongoing story charts its votes on the record.

entries.title: Follow one member, bill, agency or story
entries.summary: Each member of Congress, bill, federal agency and tracked story has its own feed of votes, actions, rules and updates, so a reader can follow just one without an account.

entries.title: Comment periods lead with rules
entries.summary: Agency pages and Explore list proposed and final rules first, fold paperwork renewals apart, and show each abstract's first sentence and the days left.

entries.title: The Supreme Court, case by case
entries.summary: The Court page puts the justices on one left to right line, shows how often each pair votes together, and lists each decision's majority and dissent; each justice's page lists every case.

entries.title: Permanent document links that cite the source
entries.summary: Each Explore document has a permanent address from its official identifier, cites the body that issued it, and is found first by its docket or Record page.

entries.title: A representative's seat on the ballot
entries.summary: Every House member's profile links the race for the member's own seat, and says plainly, with the source, when the member is not among the seat's confirmed nominees.

entries.title: How a bill got there
entries.summary: Each bill page maps its path from introduction to law with dates, says how each chamber passed it, by roll call, voice vote or unanimous consent, and explains the procedural steps in plain words.

entries.title: What each amendment vote was about
entries.summary: A vote on an amendment now quotes the amendment's official purpose from the record, and each roll call page shows the chamber as a seat chart, one dot per member.

entries.title: Where to register, and by when
entries.summary: Each state page opens with when registration closes, the days left and a link to register with the state, and the elections page lists states closing in the next 10 days.

entries.title: The seat map checked against the count
entries.summary: Once a state lists a race's count as official, the archive checks it against the seat map's pre-election ranges, lists every miss, and maps how far each seat swung from its usual vote.

entries.title: Election calendar
entries.summary: Every federal election date and filing deadline in one place, with each special election, each vacant seat in Congress and the next dates for every state.

entries.title: Special elections and counts
entries.summary: Each special election the FEC lists is kept on the site, and its count is read from the state's own results feed on election night, as the general's is.

entries.title: Every section, one menu
entries.summary: The main menu, the footer and each section's tabs now list every section and page the same way, with a live figure beside each section.

entries.title: Election archive
entries.summary: Each general election stays on the site once held: its ballot, the candidates as printed, each race's count as the state reported it, and the measures, quoted.

entries.title: Presidential nominations
entries.summary: Every presidential nomination sent to the Senate, with its status, how long confirmation took and the roll calls that name it.

entries.title: Election map
entries.summary: How each Senate and House seat usually votes, a range for the margin from the cycle's polls where a seat has any, and where the two disagree, with no race called.

entries.title: Federal agencies
entries.summary: Every agency the Federal Register lists, with its spending from USAspending.gov, the rules it proposes and issues, and its open comment periods.

entries.title: Committee meetings and reports
entries.summary: Every Senate and House committee meeting and committee report this Congress, as the Daily Digest printed each one, found by committee, word or bill number.

entries.title: A page for every roll call
entries.summary: Each Senate and House roll call, nominations included, has a page of its own, linked from every list of votes.

entries.title: A second district lean, computed here
entries.summary: A partisan lean for every House district worked out with Cook's formula from open precinct returns, shown beside Cook's figure, with CSV and JSON downloads.

entries.title: What changed on the new House maps
entries.summary: For each district on a redrawn map, where its residents lived before, how its partisan lean moved, and the act or court order behind the map.

entries.title: Votes with the president
entries.summary: How often each member of Congress votes with the president's stated positions on bills, beside the rate the member's seat predicts.

entries.title: How often two members vote alike
entries.summary: Pick any two members of Congress to see how often the two voted the same way this Congress.

entries.title: Call your members from an issue
entries.summary: Pick a state on an Action Center issue for the office phone of each member, each member's votes on the issue's roll calls, and a call script.

entries.title: Voter calendar
entries.summary: Registration, early voting and mail-ballot deadlines for every state, read from each state's election office, on each state's ballot page.

entries.title: Find a House member by town
entries.summary: Find the House member for a city, town or county by picking a state and typing a place name, with no address asked for.
